BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL PASO                        )
 ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF ITS RETAIL                        ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 ELECTRIC RATES PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE                           )
 NO. 317                                                            )

    ORDER GRANTING MOTION TO WITHDRAW CONFIDENTIAL TESTIMONY
                      AND REFILE TESTIMONY

        THIS MATTER comes before Keven Gedko and Nicholas Rossi, hearing examiners for

the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”), upon the Regents of New

Mexico State University’s (“NMSU”) Motion to Withdraw Confidential Testimony and File

Amended Public Testimony of Michael P. Gorman on Behalf of NMSU (“Motion”), filed on

October 28, 2026. Being duly informed, the Hearing Examiners FIND and CONCLUDE:

        1.       On October 28, 2026, NMSU filed its Motion, requesting it be allowed to withdraw

the Confidential Testimony of Michael P. Gorman and its Confidential Exhibit MPG-21

(“Confidential Testimony”), and file an amended version of the Public Direct Testimony and

Exhibits of Michael P. Gorman that was filed on October 23, 2026.1

        2.       The Motion explains that the amended testimony “would remove the redactions on

pages 22, 25, and 27 of Mr. Gorman’s [Confidential Testimony] in light of the Stipulation that

EPE waives confidentiality of the redacted material and EPE will not challenge its admission into

the evidentiary record in this case,” 2 and asserts that the filing of the amended, non-redacted

version of Mr. Gorman’s public testimony would simplify and clarify the record, and avoid

procedural and evidentiary complexities during the public hearing in this matter.3




1 Motion (Oct. 28, 2026) at 1.

2 Id.

3 Id.
                BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Granting Motion to Withdraw and Refile Testimony    Docket No. 25-00082-UT



        3.      The Motion is unopposed.

        4.      The Hearing Examiners find there is good cause to grant the Motion.

        5.      The Hearing Examiners also find that the Motion does not directly address

Confidential Exhibit MPG-21. However, Confidential Exhibit MPG-21 is referenced as a footnote

to the text on pages 22 and 27 that NMSU requests to refile in unredacted form, and provides the

basis for the unredacted text that will be filed.

        6.      The Hearing Examiners therefore understand that NMSU’s filing of Mr. Gorman’s

amended testimony should include Exhibit MPG-21 and the citations to that exhibit that exist in

the Confidential Testimony.

        7.      Further, the Confidential Testimony has not been admitted to an official record in

this docket. Filings are not removed from e360 once they are filed, but that does not mean they are

part of an official record. For the purpose of granting the Motion, the Confidential Testimony being

“withdrawn” means that it will remain in the Commission’s e360 filing system but will not be

proposed for admission into the official record in this docket.

        8.      Finally, the amended testimony should be filed by November 19, 2026, so that

rebuttal testimony that is filed on November 20, 2026 may reference the amended testimony.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

        A.      The Motion is GRANTED.

        B.      The Confidential Direct Testimony and Exhibits of Michael P. Gorman are

WITHDRAWN.

        C.      By November 19, 2026, NMSU shall file an amended version of the Public Direct

Testimony and Exhibits of Michael P. Gorman that includes the unredacted text that was redacted



                                                    2

in the Confidential Testimony, as well Exhibit MPG-21 and citations to that exhibit. In the

alternative, if the Stipulation does not encompass Exhibit MPG-21, by November 19, 2026, NMSU

and EPE shall file an explanation of how to enact the agreement they have reached that takes into

account Exhibit MPG-21.

    ISSUED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on November 18, 2026.



                           NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
